content: 1. Aluminum hydroxide and dolutegravir: Aluminum hydroxide reduces the plasma levels and efficacy of dolutegravir by binding to cations in the gastrointestinal (GI) tract. To minimize this interaction, administer dolutegravir at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after taking aluminum hydroxide-containing medications. If possible, consider alternative therapies. 2. Doxercalciferol and magnesium hydroxide: Doxercalciferol increases magnesium hydroxide levels by enhancing its GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral formulations of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown but likely minor. 3. Magnesium hydroxide and doxycycline: Magnesium hydroxide decreases doxycycline levels by inhibiting its GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. Avoid co-administration or separate doses by at least 2 hours. Consider alternative therapies if necessary. 4. Aluminum hydroxide and doxycycline: Aluminum hydroxide similarly reduces doxycycline levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. Avoid co-administration or separate doses by at least 2 hours. 5. Drospirenone and magnesium hydroxide: Drospirenone increases magnesium hydroxide levels by reducing renal clearance. The clinical significance is unknown but likely minor. 6. Magnesium hydroxide and eltrombopag: Magnesium hydroxide decreases eltrombopag levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. Co-administration is contraindicated. Separate doses by at least 4 hours. 7. Aluminum hydroxide and eltrombopag: Aluminum hydroxide also reduces eltrombopag levels via the same mechanism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Separate doses by at least 4 hours. 8. Aluminum hydroxide and elvitegravir: Aluminum hydroxide decreases elvitegravir levels by forming ionic complexes in the GI tract, not by altering gastric pH. Separate doses by at least 2 hours. Monitor closely. 9. Aluminum hydroxide and elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF: Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of this combination therapy by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. Separate doses by at least 2 hours and monitor closely. 10. Aluminum hydroxide and enalapril: Aluminum hydroxide reduces the efficacy of enalapril through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Aluminum hydroxide and ephedrine: Aluminum hydroxide increases ephedrine levels by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urinary environment. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Aluminum hydroxide and erythromycin (various formulations): Aluminum hydroxide increases erythromycin levels (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, stearate) through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Aluminum hydroxide and esmolol: Aluminum hydroxide decreases esmolol levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. Separate doses by at least 2 hours and monitor closely. 14. Estradiol and magnesium hydroxide: Estradiol decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by shifting magnesium from the blood to tissue storage. The clinical significance is unknown but likely minor. 15. Estrogens (conjugated, synthetic, esterified) and magnesium hydroxide: These agents decrease magnesium hydroxide levels via the same mechanism as estradiol. The clinical significance is unknown but likely minor. 16. Ethacrynic acid and magnesium hydroxide: Ethacrynic acid decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance is unknown but likely minor. 17. Aluminum hydroxide and ethambutol: Aluminum hydroxide increases ethambutol levels by cation binding in the GI tract. Avoid administering aluminum hydroxide-containing antacids for at least 4 hours after ethambutol dosing. Monitor closely. 18. Aluminum hydroxide and etidronate: Aluminum hydroxide decreases etidronate levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. Separate doses by at least 2 hours and monitor closely. 19. Aluminum hydroxide and ferric maltol: Aluminum hydroxide decreases ferric maltol levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Aluminum hydroxide and ferrous salts (fumarate, gluconate, sulfate): Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of these iron salts by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Aluminum hydroxide and flecainide: Aluminum hydroxide increases flecainide levels by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urinary environment. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Magnesium hydroxide and fleroxacin: Magnesium hydroxide decreases fleroxacin levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. Avoid co-administration or separate doses by at least 2 hours. 23. Aluminum hydroxide and fosamprenavir: Aluminum hydroxide decreases fosamprenavir levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Aluminum hydroxide and fosinopril: Aluminum hydroxide reduces fosinopril efficacy through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Furosemide and magnesium hydroxide: Furosemide decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance is unknown but likely minor. 26. Aluminum hydroxide and gabapentin (including enacarbil): Aluminum hydroxide decreases gabapentin levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. Separate doses by at least 2 hours and monitor closely. 27. Aluminum hydroxide and gefitinib: Aluminum hydroxide decreases gefitinib levels by increasing gastric pH. Separate doses by at least 6 hours and monitor closely. 28. Magnesium hydroxide and gemifloxacin: Magnesium hydroxide decreases gemifloxacin levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. Avoid co-administration or separate doses by at least 2 hours. 29. Aluminum hydroxide and gentamicin: Gentamicin decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance is unknown but likely minor. 30. Aluminum hydroxide and glipizide/glyburide: Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels of these agents by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Hydrochlorothiazide and magnesium hydroxide: Hydrochlorothiazide decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance is unknown but likely minor. 32. Aluminum hydroxide and ibandronate: Aluminum hydroxide decreases ibandronate levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Magnesium hydroxide and ibandronate: Magnesium hydroxide decreases ibandronate levels via the same mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown but likely minor. 34. Aluminum hydroxide and imidapril: Aluminum hydroxide reduces imidapril efficacy through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Indapamide and magnesium hydroxide: Indapamide decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance is unknown but likely minor. 36. Aluminum hydroxide and indinavir: Aluminum hydroxide decreases indinavir levels by increasing gastric pH. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 37. Aluminum hydroxide and itraconazole: Aluminum hydroxide decreases itraconazole levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Administer acid-neutralizing medications at least 2 hours before or after itraconazole dosing. Monitor closely. 38. Aluminum hydroxide and ketoconazole: Aluminum hydroxide decreases ketoconazole levels by increasing gastric pH. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 39. Aluminum hydroxide and labetalol: Aluminum hydroxide decreases labetalol levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate doses by at least 2 hours and monitor closely. 40. Aluminum hydroxide and lactulose: Aluminum hydroxide reduces lactulose efficacy through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Lanthanum carbonate and antacids (aluminum hydroxide, magnesium hydroxide): These agents bind cations in the GI tract. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or after lanthanum carbonate dosing. Monitor closely. 42. Aluminum hydroxide and ledipasvir/sofosbuvir: Aluminum hydroxide decreases ledipasvir levels by reducing its solubility as gastric pH increases. Separate doses by at least 4 hours and monitor closely. 43. Magnesium hydroxide and levofloxacin: Magnesium hydroxide decreases levofloxacin levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Avoid co-administration or separate doses by at least 2 hours. 44. Aluminum hydroxide and levofloxacin: Aluminum hydroxide decreases levofloxacin levels via the same mechanism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 45. Aluminum hydroxide and levoketoconazole: Aluminum hydroxide decreases levoketoconazole levels by increasing gastric pH. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 46. Aluminum hydroxide and lisdexamfetamine: Aluminum hydroxide increases lisdexamfetamine levels by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urinary environment. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Aluminum hydroxide and lisinopril: Aluminum hydroxide reduces lisinopril efficacy through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Mannitol and magnesium hydroxide: Mannitol decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance is unknown but likely minor. 49. Aluminum hydroxide and memantine: Aluminum hydroxide increases memantine levels by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urinary environment. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Aluminum hydroxide and mesalamine: Aluminum hydroxide alters salicylate levels depending on the dose. Salicylate levels increase at moderate doses and decrease at high doses due to increased renal excretion. Monitor closely. 51. Mestranol and magnesium hydroxide: Mestranol decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by shifting magnesium from the blood to tissue storage. The clinical significance is unknown but likely minor. 52. Aluminum hydroxide and methscopolamine: Aluminum hydroxide decreases methscopolamine levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral formulations. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Methyclothiazide and magnesium hydroxide: Methyclothiazide decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance is unknown but likely minor. 54. Aluminum hydroxide and methylphenidate: Aluminum hydroxide alters the release of extended-release methylphenidate capsules (e.g., Ritalin LA) due to pH-dependent characteristics. Separate doses to avoid interaction. 55. Metolazone and magnesium hydroxide: Metolazone decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance is unknown but likely minor. 56. Aluminum hydroxide and metoprolol: Aluminum hydroxide decreases metoprolol levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate doses by at least 2 hours and monitor closely. 57. Aluminum hydroxide and mexiletine: Aluminum hydroxide increases mexiletine levels by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urinary environment. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Magnesium hydroxide and minocycline: Magnesium hydroxide decreases minocycline levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Avoid co-administration or separate doses by at least 2 hours. 59. Aluminum hydroxide and minocycline: Aluminum hydroxide decreases minocycline levels via the same mechanism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. 60. Aluminum hydroxide and moexipril: Aluminum hydroxide reduces moexipril efficacy through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 61. Magnesium hydroxide and moxifloxacin: Magnesium hydroxide decreases moxifloxacin levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Avoid co-administration or separate doses by at least 2 hours. 62. Aluminum hydroxide and moxifloxacin: Aluminum hydroxide decreases moxifloxacin levels via the same mechanism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies.
